fullText:
The Kansas City Chiefs acquired OL Josh Ezeudu from the New York Giants for a 2028 seventh-round pick before their final preseason game.

The Chiefs have had a very real concern about their offensive line all preseason, with a severe lack of depth behind their lead options, Kingsley Suamataia and Trey Smith.

With the offensive line playing an integral role in the success of the quarterback, the Chiefs have added reinforcements to their shallow o-line for Patrick Mahomes' protection.

ESPN reported the Chiefs' acquisition of Josh Ezeudu from the Giants to bolster their offensive line for a low cost.

Ezeudu is a 26-year-old former third-round pick who has appeared in 33 NFL games over his career. He's made only 10 starts and missed the entirety of last season with a calf injury.

Ezeudu can play as both a left and right guard, and has played at left tackle as well, showing he has the varied skill set a backup needs to fill in wherever required on the o-line.

That versatility can also give the Chiefs the room they need to develop a young option like Kahlil Benson in his preferred role rather than making him learn new styles on the fly as a floating backup.

The Chiefs' potential five-man offensive line of LT Josh Simmons, LG Suamataia, C Creed Humphrey, RG Smith, and RT Jaylon Moore can be elite, but they need to have strong backup options like Ezeudu to step up when required.

Their current backup options have been underwhelming throughout camp, so Ezeudu is a low-cost, high-upside swing for them.

Even a bad version of him would fit as a backup OL member, but even above-average production could make him a key backup.

The Chiefs need extra protection for Mahomes this season, especially early in the season, as he has to get comfortable after returning from a torn ACL.

This will in turn affect the kind of service options like Travis Kelce receive in what might be a retirement season for him.

Ezeudu has the talent and the size; it's just a question of him staying healthy enough to build momentum over the season and showcase his full strengths. If he does that, the Chiefs will be much better than anticipated.

title: Retiring Wawrinka 'forever grateful' to US Open despite no wildcard
description: Stan Wawrinka says his US Open triumph will "forever be one of the greatest moments of my life" after missing out on a wildcard for a farewell appearance in New York.
fullText:
Stan Wawrinka says his US Open triumph will "forever be one of the greatest moments of my life" after missing out on a wildcard for a farewell appearance in New York.

The 41-year-old will retire at the end of year and was given a wildcard for this year's Australian Open and Wimbledon, while reaching the French Open main-draw on ranking.

He reached the third round in Melbourne and lost a pair of entertaining first-round matches in Paris and Wimbledon respectively.

The US Open has received some criticism for its decision not to award a wildcard to 2016 champion Wawrinka, who did not enter qualifying despite being inside the cut-off.

The United States Tennis Association (USTA) says it does not comment on wildcard decisions.

Despite not receiving a wildcard, Wawrinka thanked the US Open and the city of New York in a social media post.

"When I first arrived in New York from a small farming village in Switzerland, everything felt too big. The city. The noise. The energy. The crowds. The lights," the Swiss wrote.

"But, year after year, New York slowly became one of my favourite places in the world.

"This city challenged me. It pushed me. It brought something out of me that few places ever could.

"I experienced some of the strongest emotions of my career here. The battles, the late nights, the incredible atmosphere, the love from the crowd… memories that will stay with me forever.

"Winning the US Open, in the city that never sleeps, will forever be one of the greatest moments of my life."

Alcaraz and Williams thrill in US Open mixed doubles

GB's Dart and Jones advance in US Open qualifying

Wawrinka was one of the few players to win major singles trophies during the 'Big Three' era of Novak Djokovic, Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer.

The former world number three won the 2014 Australian Open and 2015 French Open before triumphing at the US Open 10 years ago.

He made 17 appearances in the men's singles in New York since making his main-draw debut in 2005.

Wawrinka's coach, Magnus Norman, wrote on Instagram: "We pushed to play one last Grand Slam at 41 years of age but we just came up short.

"It sure hurts but thanks for all the beautiful memories on and off the court together with you and the team in New York for the past 13 years."

Wildcards are given to players who did not qualify automatically for the tournament by ranking. Wawrinka has fallen outside the top 100 after struggling with injuries and form in recent years.

Switzerland also does not host a Grand Slam, with tournaments reserving reciprocal wildcards for one another.

France's Gael Monfils, who is also retiring this season, was given a wildcard through the French Tennis Federation, which organises the French Open.

Reciprocal wildcards are assigned by the national federations and not the US Open.

The US Open gets under way on Sunday, 30 August at Flushing Meadows.

Other than the reciprocal wildcards the USTA reserves for French and Australian players, the other six wildcards for both the men's and women's singles went to Americans.

The USTA organises and bankrolls the US Open, and would argue it has every right to put its own players first.

But when a charismatic champion like Wawrinka is not given the chance to say a proper farewell to the event he won in 2016, then the sport as a whole suffers.

Home players dominate the list of wildcards at all the Grand Slams, but the Australian Open found space for Stan Wawrinka and Venus Williams, while Wimbledon offered wildcards to Wawrinka, Grigor Dimitrov, Serena Williams and French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska.

title: Alcaraz and Williams thrill in brief but bright US Open mixed doubles showing

fullText:

That was how Carlos Alcaraz settled back into competitive action at the US Open, partnering the American great as she returned to her home slam after a four-year absence.

The tournament's revamped mixed doubles format has attracted criticism for favouring the allure of the sport's top singles stars at the expense of established doubles players.

But the crowds turned out and produced a terrific atmosphere for the tournament's headline act, with about 15,000 people packed inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.

All four doubles specialist pairings lost to a team of singles players on Tuesday, while Alcaraz and Williams fell in the quarter-finals.

Seven-time major winner Alcaraz was playing his first competitive match since April after injuring his wrist, while 23-time Grand Slam champion Williams was competing in New York for the first time since she "evolved away" from tennis in 2022.

The pair were greeted by huge cheers and were roared on throughout their opening 5-3 4-1 win against Great Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and New Zealand's Erin Routliffe.

The 44-year-old Williams won the US Open mixed doubles title in its original format alongside Max Mirnyi in 1998 - five years before Alcaraz was born.

Almost 30 years later, Williams still had the competitive desire. She and Alcaraz enjoyed the occasion, playing with smiles on their faces and roaring each other on after winning a point.

Interviewed during a change of ends, Alcaraz said: "I'm playing next to the one and only Serena Williams, so what else can I do? Just enjoy and try to do the things she told me to do."

Their partnership improved rapidly in their first match as they won eight of the final nine games to seal victory.

However, they were denied a place in Wednesday's semi-finals by Italy's world number six Flavio Cobolli and Swiss team-mate Belinda Bencic, who won 5-4 (7-4) 4-1.

GB's Dart and Jones advance in US Open qualifying

Wawrinka 'grateful' despite no US Open wildcard

While Williams will not contest the singles at the US Open - she has not competed in that format since injuring her knee at Wimbledon - Tuesday's matches provided the returning Alcaraz with valuable court time.

The Spaniard admitted he felt nervous before stepping out on the court - in part due to partnering six-time US Open women's singles champion Williams.

"I think everyone could see I was really nervous, I double-faulted on the first point," Alcaraz said after their opening win.

"I was out for almost five months and I almost forgot how it feels stepping out on the court once again.

"It [took] just a couple of games [to settle] and she made it very easy for me to enjoy it and try to go for it."

For Williams, a return to the Arthur Ashe Stadium was something she did not believe would come around again.

"It's always amazing to be here. I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said.

"It was just a really cool moment. I never thought this would happen."

The controversial revamped mixed doubles format, introduced last year, pits established doubles players against some of the sport's biggest singles stars.

The tournament takes place the week before the singles draw gets under way and allows direct entry into the main draw for top-ranked singles players and wildcards.

Established doubles players such as Britons Glasspool and Henry Patten had to come through two qualifying rounds on Monday.

Top-ranked players Patten and Katerina Siniakova advanced to the quarter-finals before losing to husband-and-wife duo Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina.

Discussing their dynamic, with a semi-final against Cobolli and Bencic to come, Frenchman Monfils said: "I'm a big fan of her game and mentality. Sometimes I think she's ice and I'm the fire.

"We needed to the find the balance. We did today."

The other semi-final will see Russians Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev face Czech pair Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik.

It was not all plain sailing for the leading singles players, with men's 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic and women's world number one Aryna Sabalenka suffering an early exit at the hands of Patten and Siniakova.

Sabalenka and Djokovic lasted just 49 minutes, but this was otherwise a day where the singles stars edged out the doubles specialists.

With none of the four doubles pairs making it to the last four, the USTA has the sort of semi-final line up it envisaged when deciding to reinvent the mixed doubles 12 months ago.

Sabalenka and Djokovic turned out to be a very brief experiment. The other marquee pairing of Williams and Alcaraz lasted longer, with Williams in particular catching the eye in their first round win.

But with Alcaraz looking increasingly rusty in the quarter-final, Cobolli and Bencic won convincingly.

The Spaniard was wearing a compression sleeve on his right arm, and the skin fade of earlier in the year has been replaced by a mop of black hair.

This was useful court time for him, but did not really tell us anything about his chances of remaining in New York for the singles final in just under three weeks time.

title: NY Rangers Could Have a Surprising Roster Cut Coming
description: The NY Rangers could end up with a relatively complex roster decision at training camp this fall, as surprising as it may be. The post NY Rangers Could Have a Surprising Roster Cut Coming appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The NY Rangers could be facing a rather surprising roster decision when training camp arrives later this fall.

That roster decision could lead to a once blue line mainstay on the outside looking in: Urho Vaakanainen.

That might seem implausible considering Vaakanainen is a perfectly capable NHL defenseman. But that's exactly what makes this situation somewhat complex. The Rangers have added more competition to their blue line, and suddenly there may not be enough room for everyone.

The NY Rangers brought in Marcus Pettersson and Sean Durzi, while players such as Matthew Robertson and Drew Fortescue are also competing for opportunities. Scott Morrow in particular is expected to challenge for a spot on the NHL roster.

Vaakanainen could ultimately be the unfortunate victim of it.

This isn't necessarily an indictment of his playing ability. It could simply be about the Rangers deciding that younger players need the opportunity to show what they can do. And that could leave Vaakanainen squeezed out of the lineup.

The problem for Vaakanainen is that he isn't exactly a stalwart for the NY Rangers

He's a reliable defensive option, but he isn't likely to provide the offensive upside of some of the Rangers' other options. He's also not the kind of physical presence that makes him indispensable in a depth role.

That makes him relatively easy to push down the depth chart. Petterson and Durzi have already done that.

Morrow, meanwhile, represents something the NY Rangers don't have nearly as much of with their veteran defensemen: Upside expectations.

If the Blueshirts believe Morrow can eventually become a legitimate top-four blueliner, giving him NHL minutes becomes much more valuable than continuing to give playing time to a 27-year-old depth player.

The same logic applies to Vincent Iorio. Yes, he's a good depth piece, but not quite the piece that would transform the NY Rangers' defense corps.

The Blueshirts don't need to know what Vaakanainen can become. They already have a pretty good idea.

They need to figure out what their younger defensemen can become. That's why Vaakanainen could be the odd man out despite being perfectly serviceable.

And there is another issue. If the Rangers decide they want to give one of their younger defensemen a permanent NHL opportunity, someone has to go. Vaakanainen is simply one of the easiest players to identify as the expendable piece.

It's harsh, but that's how roster construction works.

NY Rangers Biggest Need Is Also Most Obvious One

Of course, there is another possibility. Vaakanainen could remain with the team.

The NY Rangers might decide that having a reliable seventh or eighth defenseman is more important than forcing a younger player into the lineup before he's ready. That could leave Vaakanainen on the roster, but his role would probably be significantly diminished. Instead of being counted on for regular minutes, he could become the insurance policy.

That's actually a pretty valuable role over an 82-game season. Injuries happen, players struggle, meaning that someone eventually needs to step into the lineup. Having a defenseman who already knows how to play at the NHL level gives the Rangers some protection against those problems.

And if Vaakanainen is willing to accept that role, keeping him around makes sense.

The question is whether the NY Rangers believe the roster spot is better used on a younger player. That's what makes this situation worth watching. Vaakanainen isn't necessarily being pushed out because he's bad. He could be pushed out because the blueshirts have decided that the future is more important than squeezing a few more minutes out of a proven depth defenseman.

And if that's the decision the organization makes, it would be one of the more surprising roster cuts of training camp.

The New York Jets actually look like they have some genuine momentum. After dropping their preseason opener to Tampa Bay, Aaron Glenn's team responded with a statement performance in Pittsburgh. Suddenly, the competition for roster spots feels considerably more consequential. Geno Smith has already demonstrated that the offense can operate efficiently under Frank Reich. There defense has generated pressure and turnovers. With one preseason game remaining against the Giants, the Jets must separate legitimate contributors from temporary summer standouts. This will determine which 53 players give them the best chance to compete when the games finally count.

The Jets sit at 1-1 through two preseason games. They recovered from a 24-16 home defeat against Tampa Bay with a dominant 17-0 shutout of Pittsburgh at Acrisure Stadium. The encouraging response has given Glenn's revamped squad some much-needed confidence. Smith was particularly impressive in his preseason debut. He completed all seven of his passes on a touchdown drive while operating Reich's offense with efficiency and rhythm. Meanwhile, the defense overwhelmed Pittsburgh with four sacks and two takeaways. That offered a glimpse of the aggressive identity Glenn wants to establish. The Giants now provide the final measuring stick before New York must finalize its 53-man roster.

Quarterback (2): Geno Smith, Cade Klubnik

Smith has the experience and accuracy to serve as the unquestioned starter. His early preseason performance reinforced why the Jets believe he can provide stability. Reich's system should allow Smith to operate from structure while taking advantage of his ability to make quick decisions. Klubnik earns the backup spot. He gives New York a developmental option with enough mobility to expand the offense when necessary. The Jets ultimately cannot afford to devote a third roster spot to the position.

Running Back (5): Breece Hall, Braelon Allen, Isaiah Davis, Kene Nwangwu, Andrew Beck

Hall remains the centerpiece because of his home-run potential. The Jets have every reason to maximize his touches. Allen provides physicality and complementary early-down work. Davis gives the team another capable runner. Nwangwu's value extends beyond the backfield because of his special-teams ability. Beck's fullback versatility makes him particularly useful in short-yardage packages. It is an unusually deep group, but every member offers a distinct role.

Wide Receiver (6): Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Omar Cooper Jr, Tim Patrick, Arian Smith, Isaiah Williams

Wilson should remain the primary target in Reich's passing attack. His ability to win at multiple levels gives Smith a reliable option. Mitchell brings size and vertical ability. Patrick supplies veteran experience and contested-catch reliability. Cooper and Arian Smith add explosiveness. Williams provides versatility from multiple alignments.

Tight End (3): Mason Taylor, Kenyon Sadiq, Jelani Woods

Taylor projects as an important receiving component. Sadiq adds athleticism and the ability to threaten defenses vertically. Woods provides a massive target and a useful option in the red zone.

Offensive Line (9): Olu Fashanu, Dylan Parham, Josh Myers, Joe Tippmann, Armand Membou, Max Mitchell, Chukwuma Okorafor, Xavier Newman, Anez Cooper

Fashanu anchors the left side. Membou handles the right tackle position. Myers gives the interior a veteran presence at center. Parham and Tippmann complete the projected starting configuration. The depth is arguably just as important. Mitchell's ability to play multiple positions, Okorafor's tackle experience, and Newman's interior versatility provide insurance against potential injuries.

Defensive line (5): T'Vondre Sweat, Harrison Phillips, David Onyemata, Jowon Briggs, Darrell Jackson Jr

Sweat and Phillips provide substantial size and power. Onyemata adds veteran savvy and pass-rushing experience. Briggs offers rotational flexibility, with Jackson providing additional depth. The objective is clear: force opposing offenses to account for the interior before they can attack the Jets' edge rushers.

EDGE (5): David Bailey, Will McDonald IV, Joseph Ossai, Kingsley Enagbare, Nate Lynn

McDonald is the explosive pass-rushing threat capable of changing games. Bailey and Ossai provide additional pressure packages. Enagbare brings versatility and experience, and Lynn rounds out the rotation.

Linebacker (4): Demario Davis, Jamien Sherwood, Francisco "Kiko" Mauigoa, Marcelino McCrary-Ball

Davis supplies the veteran leadership and football intelligence. Sherwood complements him with athleticism and range. Mauigoa and McCrary-Ball provide younger rotational options. The Jets do not need this group to dominate statistically if the defensive line and secondary can consistently create favorable situations.

Cornerback (6): Brandon Stephens, Nahshon Wright, Jarvis Brownlee Jr, Azareye'h Thomas, D'Angelo Ponds, Qwan'tez Stiggers

Stephens provides experience on the perimeter. Wright adds another lengthy coverage option. Brownlee and Thomas give the Jets additional physicality. Ponds and Stiggers provide depth and developmental upside.

Safety (5): Minkah Fitzpatrick, Andre Cisco, Dane Belton, Malachi Moore, Samuel Womack III

Fitzpatrick gives Glenn the freedom to move him around the formation. Cisco brings playmaking ability. Belton, Moore, and Womack provide rotational and special-teams value.

Kicker: Jason Sanders
Punter: Austin McNamara
Long Snapper: Thomas Hennessy.

Sanders gives the Jets a proven option at kicker. McNamara handles punting and holding duties. Hennessy provides continuity at long snapper. With the rest of the roster undergoing significant transition, maintaining stability here is particularly valuable.

The Jets' projected roster reflects a team attempting to establish a completely different identity. Smith and Hall provide recognizable offensive pillars. Wilson gives the passing game a legitimate focal point. The combination of Fitzpatrick, Davis, and an aggressive front gives Glenn the ingredients for a physical defense.

The biggest question is whether the depth chart can translate the optimism of August into sustained regular-season performance. For a Jets organization attempting to turn encouraging flashes into meaningful progress, the final 53-man roster may be the first real blueprint of what this new era intends to become.

title: Giants Give Positive Injury Update on WR Malik Nabers
description: The New York Giants gave a positive injury update on superstar wide receiver Malik Nabers. The post Giants Give Positive Injury Update on WR Malik Nabers appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Even with 1 massive story after another for the New York Giants this offseason — including hiring a new head coach and trading away a 1st-round pick — the biggest story of them all might still be the health of superstar wide receiver Malik Nabers.

The most encouraging sign for Nabers came on Monday, when head coach John Harbaugh told the assembled media, "It's reasonable to assume" Nabers will play in the season opener barring any setbacks with his surgically repaired knee.

Nabers had 109 receptions for 1,204 yards and 7 touchdowns in 15 games as a rookie in 2024 but tore his ACL just 4 games into the 2025 regular season.

The Giants host the Cowboys for a primetime Sunday Night Football game in Week 1.

"John Harbaugh isn't ready to make any blanket statements on Malik Nabers for Week 1. But he did say … he's trending towards being ready for the Cowboys," ESPN's Jordan Raanan wrote on his official X account.

That wasn't the only positive step Nabers took toward rejoining the team on Monday.

"Another step for Malik Nabers and the Giants: He shed the red jersey and took part in 7-on-7 & 11-on-11," The New York Post's Connor Hughes wrote on his official X account. "He wasn't full (worked in for reps), but a step in right direction. He made a nice grab diving back for the ball on an intermediate route/curl. The Giants were without pads today, so not full contact in that sense, but a "contact" day for Nabers. Again … Week 1 looks good."

While Nabers still doesn't have a timetable for when he might return, he dismissed a question from reporters on Friday about if and when he might be able to return to the player he was as a rookie — although not dismissed in the way you might think.

"I have extreme confidence in myself," Nabers said. "And I not gonna put myself in any spot where I'm not gonna be better than what I was before. So I don't see myself being what I was before, what y'all saw my rookie year. I felt like that was basic … I hold myself to a very high standard, and I feel like that high standard, you're going to see it sooner or later."

The 1st hint Nabers might be ready for the season opener came when he avoided starting the season on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) List and has been running routes at full speed in individual drills.

"Giants place three players on the PUP list in advance of veterans reporting for training camp next week … and Malik Nabers is not one of them," USA Today's Art Stapleton wrote on his official X account on July 23. "Neither is Cam Skattebo, so flip out if you'd like."

Bleacher Report's Alex Kay put Nabers at the top of his list of "dark horse candidates" to win NFL Offensive Player of the Year in 2026.

"Despite Nabers' bursting onto the scene with one of the best rookie seasons in recent memory — he caught 109 passes for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns in 15 games — and establishing himself as one of the best receivers in the league, he only has the 19th best odds of winning Offensive Player of the Year this season," Kay wrote on July 8. "Nabers' impending return will be a massive boon for a Giants squad working to take a major step forward in 2026. The team went all-in on a regime change and roster improvements this offseason, most notably placing John Harbaugh at the head coaching reins and bolstering Jaxson Dart's protection with first-round guard Francis Mauigoa."

However, Liam Broady lost 7-6 (7-4) 6-3 against Italy's Marco Cecchinato, while Felix Gill was beaten by Italian Francesco Passaro 7-6 (7-3) 6-2.

Players must come through three rounds of qualifying to reach the singles main draw, which gets under way on Sunday.

Williams and Alcaraz to play US Open mixed doubles

Injured Sinner & Draper withdraw from US Open

China's two-time US Open quarter-finalist Zheng Qinwen, contesting a Grand Slam qualifying event for the first time since the 2022 Australian Open, defeated compatriot Xiaodi You 6-3 6-2.

The 23-year-old, who has fallen to 121st in the world since undergoing elbow surgery last year, will meet France's Clara Burel next.

The 20-year-old French Open quarter-finalist said he would require "more time to fully recover so I can compete at a high level".

In the mixed doubles competition, Britons Henry Patten and Lloyd Glasspool will both seek to beat some of the sport's biggest stars after coming through two qualifying matches on Monday.

The US Open mixed doubles was controversially revamped last year to include singles stars in a bid to attract more attention to the format.

Under the new format, the top six pairs with the best combined singles rankings received direct entry into the main draw, with another eight receiving wildcards.

The tournament now takes place over three days in the week before the main draw began, and features a shorter scoring system with only four games required to win a set in matches before the final, no 'advantage' scoring and 10-point match tie-breaks instead of a third set throughout.

Both Patten and Glasspool had to come through qualifying with their respective partners on Monday.

Patten, a two-time winner of the men's doubles competition at Wimbledon, and Czech team-mate Katerina Siniakova defeated Americans Peyton Stearns and Christian Harrison in straight sets in their second qualifying match.

Next, Patten and Siniakova - the respective men's and women's world number ones in doubles - will take on 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic and top-ranked Aryna Sabalenka in the first round of the main draw.

After defeating El Salvador's Marcelo Arevalo and France's Kristina Mladenovic, Glasspool and New Zealand's Erin Routliffe will face 23-time Grand Slam singles champion Serena Williams and seven-time major winner Carlos Alcaraz.

Alcaraz will be playing his first match in four months after recovering from a wrist injury, while Williams is making her return to the sport after a four-year absence.

fullText:

NEW YORK, Aug 23 (Reuters) - Tens of thousands of people have been evacuated this weekend from ‌the area of Reno, Nevada, and many others were under orders to leave ‌on Sunday as a wildfire reached the outskirts of the state's third-most-populous city.

About 42,000 residents have been displaced ​or are in active evacuations with an additional 45,000 in "be prepared to evacuate" status as the Hawk Fire threatened northern Reno, local officials said late Sunday morning.

Local TV footage showed flames approaching roads. In eyewitness video verified by Reuters, smoke from the hills billowed over nearby residential ‌neighborhoods.

Fire-tracking websites showed evacuation zones extending ⁠from the Sierra Nevada hills to the University of Nevada in northwest Reno.

The fire has burned 13,000 acres (5,261 hectares) so far, officials said ⁠at a press conference on Sunday. The fire was human-caused and remains under investigation, they said.

Three civilians and three first responders have been injured, said Shane Akerson, a commander leading fire and rescue ​operations.

Officials ​first received reports of a fire off Hawk ​Meadow Trail at about 11:15 a.m. ‌PDT (1815 GMT) on Saturday, said Richard Edwards, chief of Truckee Meadows Fire Protection District. Firefighters on Saturday worked amid "extreme red flag conditions," he said.

Red flag conditions are a combination of warm temperatures, very low humidity and strong winds that raise the risk of wildfires.

"We expect those same strong conditions to come back this afternoon," Edwards said on Sunday.

Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo ‌declared a state of emergency late Saturday in ​Washoe County, which includes Reno and parts of Lake ​Tahoe.

"This is an active and rapidly evolving ​situation, and I urge everyone in the affected areas to remain ‌vigilant and follow the direction of local ​officials," Lombardo said in ​a statement.

Lombardo authorized the deployment of two National Guard helicopters to help fight fires and 60 National Guard personnel to support operations with the Washoe County Sheriff's Office, ​officials said.

The Reno-Tahoe International Airport ‌remained outside the evacuation area, and commercial flights were operating normally on Sunday.

title: Did Odell Beckham let New York Giants opportunity slip through fingers?
description: New York Giants WR Odell Beckham Jr. had his moment on Saturday amid a competitive roster battle, but the ball slipped through his fingers.
fullText:
Odell Beckham Jr. had a chance to deliver a signature moment in the New York Giants' preseason game against the Miami Dolphins on Saturday, but the football slipped through his fingers on a potential touchdown that could have strengthened his case for a roster spot.

Beckham entered the contest needing to show more production after limited stats in Week 1. Late in the second quarter, he went up for a Jameis Winston pass in the end zone, secured his feet inbounds, and appeared ready to complete the score. The ball simply would not stay in his hands.

We got close but Odell Beckham Jr. dropped a touchdown pic.twitter.com/HWcnld02Ec

It would have been a difficult catch, the kind Beckham has made countless times throughout his career, yet this one got away.

Despite the drop, Beckham continued to flash the traits that made him a star. He showed impressive speed and quickness, sharp route running, and the ability to create separation. Like the previous week, he found himself wide open on multiple occasions, only to watch the ball go elsewhere.

After the game, Beckham did not hide his disappointment.

"A certain play that's going to stick with me the same way it always has all my life when you want to be great. When opportunities come your way, you've got to make the most of them," he told reporters. "Today, I feel like I let myself down and let my team down. Those are plays that I'll make, and I can't wait for the next opportunity."

Beckham refused to blame new gloves, insisting it was a play he would make "10 times out of 10." He added that he was "pissed" and that the drop would keep him up at night.

"You take it on the chin like a man. You eat it," he said.

For a veteran fighting for a place on the Giants roster, the missed touchdown represented a significant opportunity that slipped away.

title: Walking the Length of Manhattan
fullText:
Hi, I’m Craig Mod and this is Ridgeline, a newsletter about walking — mostly in Japan, but this time in NYC.

Back in May, my original NYC plan was to do five or six days of huge walks while running a pop-up newsletter — basically go walk bananas in the city. But then I stopped for a second and thought: What if I just … enjoyed NYC? And so I did. I did the thing I have a hard time doing — simply enjoying a place or trip instead of turning it into a project.

Of course I did micro walks, micro projects. I walked the Brooklyn Bridge, I sped-walked the Met, and I walked around some POPS (privately owned public spaces). Naturally, I couldn’t keep the walks entirely tiny. Buddy, and National Geographic photographer extraordinaire Michael George sent me a text: Wanna walk Manhattan top to bottom? Of course I did.

I arrived at Marble Hill–225th St. Station in not shorts. You’re not wearing shorts?! Michael screamed at me from across the street. I am a self-respecting adult male, so no — I wasn’t wearing shorts. He couldn’t believe it. He was convinced I’d die fifteen steps into the walk. I was less interested in my pants and more interested in the world’s worst-rated Starbucks around the corner. The indignation of Starbucks fanatics was off the review charts. Should we go see? I asked. Go see how terrible it could be? I was nibbling an egg-on-English muffin sandwich from a nearby Dunkin’ Donuts, also admirably terrible. When I gave my order it was as if I had defecated directly onto the cash register. The muffin was all but thrown at me. Ahh, America. I loved it.

We did not go to the world’s worst Starbucks because we had a lot of walking to do. In the end: 24.4 kilometers. Not too shabby. Knocked out in six hours. We were fairly militant about keeping the route direct since we wanted to get to Battery Park by sunset.

We began at Marble Hill to make our walk fully official — crossing the Historic Broadway Lift Bridge connecting the island of Manhattan to the wider continent.

I always forget Manhattan is technically an island. For many years I didn’t know. It feels non-islandy in the mind and myth, and given the demure nature of Spuyten Duyvil Creek, I’m shocked nobody has connected the two landmasses issometime in the last 400 years, ending Manhattan’s islandic status.

Step by step, we made our way “down” Manhattan. There were many detours we did not take. I had never been to the utterly beloved Met Cloisters (so beloved, it’s almost as if the Starbucks back across the bridge was the natural antipode to the Cloisters, as if it existed simply to balance out Cloister goodness), and going there would have made me happy, but it was also way too early in the walk for such a big stop. So the Met Cloisters stays on my “To Visit One Day” list.

Instead we strolled Highbridge Park abutting the Harlem River. In it we saw nary another human. The path gained more elevation than you’d expect, and some of the rock formations were downright Paleolithic. We did not walk the namesake High Bridge (the city’s oldest standing bridge (1848)) itself, but we walked near it.

We were making a beeline for the Morris-Jumel Mansion. Michael had planned these little stops. I was just along for the ride. The mansion was closed for renovation. Still, it was impressive from the outside — a lovely little garden out back. Built in 1765, it brought a certain bizarre countryside gravitas to the nearby meth community. You could imagine it 200 years ago, surrounded not by billions of tons of concrete but by rolling meadows. A woman was pushing a stroller around the grounds and her daughter, maybe seven or eight, was walking beside her. Nice house, huh! I said, amplifying my whiteness to a hitherto unseen degree. She just frowned and pointed to her AirPods — she was on a call, she wasn’t here for the house. I was a moron. The grounds were just a good place to walk your kid.

Directly across from the mansion was a cute block: Sylvan Terrace. New York City does this — inserts little blocks of goodness like prizes in the Cracker Jack box of ugly life. Pomander Walk is another. Emma Straub’s lovely novel, This Time Tomorrow, hinges on literal magic found on Pomander Walk. This is what these cute low-rise nooks do: They inspire awe that such things have survived the march of time, the relentless verticality of the rest of the city.

Having now seen a place of historical import, and having walked some six kilometers, I felt I was owed a good coffee. So it was that we popped into Manhattanville Coffee, which delivered the goods. The day was hot, so I ended up with three drinks before me, much to Michael’s astonishment. Three?? he said, taking a photo to memorialize the liquid opulence on which I blew my cash. Hey, I had experienced a kidney stone last year, and hydration had shot up on the list of things on which never to compromise.

Just before popping in for coffee, we had passed the cantilevered Sugar Hill Housing Development — affordable housing in an avant-garde container with a children’s museum on the first floor.

Down through Sugar Hill and Hamilton Heights, down through West Harlem alongside St. Nicholas Park we strode. The city became more city-like. Gentrification became more apparent, and by the time we were on 125th Street, just a few blocks from the Apollo Theater, you felt like you were in the hungry heart of commerce once again.

We tucked into a bodega and I ordered my favorite slap-up lunch — a turkey and cheese on an everything bagel with jalapeños and spicy mustard and tomato, with a bag of salt and vinegar chips (to be shoved into the bagel) and a sparkling water. (Almost as good as a cheese sandwich with Branston Pickle.)

We lunched al fresco in the shade near the Great Hill of Central Park, cooing over our godlike sandwiches. Around us the park thrummed with perfect parkiness. What an absolute miracle of a place, Central Park. The greenery, sure, but just the sheer resource of the space, all this space available to anyone breathing and capable of being outside. Little groups had gathered here and there, also lunching on this weekday afternoon in the sun, hot but not too hot, the Knicks having recently won, the pervasive vibes being good vibes, everyone aware of how lucky they were to be right here at this very moment. We felt that luck.

We stuck to the west edge of the park, passing the reservoir, down down past the 90s, the 80s, past the American Museum of Natural History, past the Ladies Pavilion and the Lake, into Strawberry Fields thinking about Lennon having been shot just a hundred meters away in front of The Dakota. The farther south we got, the more intense became the park activity. Rollerbladers, horses, bikes of all types — recumbent and carbon time trialers and Citi Bikes and Bromptons — whizzed past. We passed Tavern on the Green and Umpire Rock and finally were ejected onto Columbus Circle and the mad world of Midtown tourists and office workers.

Engulfed. We were engulfed in crowds, moving through the sectors of Manhattan we both knew best. We wiggled down Broadway to Times Square because why not. More people. All weirdly tame though, everyone a bit languid from the heat perhaps. We continued to blast down past Penn Station, sticking mostly to Seventh Ave since we were a good eighteen kilometers or so in and were looking forward to hitting Battery Park and detours were not on our minds. We could have walked by the Flatiron and through Madison Square Park (ahh the original Shake Shack, hello, I remember visiting you many lives back), and then through Union Square for a quick spot of people watching (hello Reinhold!), then over through Washington Square Park and past the chess games and then into Greenwich Village past the Comedy Cellar, through that jumble into SoHo, but we didn’t. We just stuck to Seventh Ave. Through the West Village we went (hello Three Lives and Company, the greatest of bookshops) down into those haunted hinterlands between the West Village and TriBeCa, a desolate stretch of woebegone blocks with no real texture or life. But then, the Ghostbusters firehouse appears, and you’re in the heart of quiet TriBeCa, past Walker’s and Gotan and soon enough the Oculus — strangely appealing in its spinal boniness, an inversion of the dark, austere holes of infinite falling water across the street.

Sure, there’s a better walk down through the Financial District, but we didn’t care. We wanted The Battery and we wanted it now. And we got it. Into the park and past the merry-go-round and finally to water’s edge. The Statue of Liberty just a little blip out on the horizon. It felt good. We did it — we walked the island. We sat in some comfy chairs in the shade and a friend of Michael’s passed by. Hi, we just walked from Marble Hill. Oh?

It was early evening. We made better time than expected but were still worn down. We decided on dinner at the Dead Rabbit on the edge of the warren of buildings that is the Financial District. The so-called Fraunces Tavern Block — a trapezoid bounded by Pearl Street, Broad Street, Water Street, and Coenties Slip — was the last of the original-scale Manhattan south of Wall Street. Five-story brick warehouses, laid out back when Pearl Street was the shoreline. The Dead Rabbit’s building is from 1828. Most everything around here burned in the Great Fire of 1835. In 1977, this block went on the National Register and became an official historic district.

Into this improbable timeslip we stepped. We ate oysters. They felt well earned. Around us a strange collection of tourists and bankers hooted and hollered over the TVs and music. The plan was to do many more walks like this around NYC. Next year I will.

title: New York Times loses defamation suit, ordered to pay $9.25M to former Alabama basketball player
description: An Alabama jury awarded Kai Spears $9.25 million in damages after finding The New York Times defamed the former University of Alabama basketball player.
fullText:
The New York Times was defeated in a defamation lawsuit Thursday brought by a former college basketball player and ordered to pay millions in damages.

An Alabama jury ruled the Times defamed Kai Spears, then an 18-year-old freshman walk-on basketball player for the University of Alabama's Crimson Tide, who was swept up in a 2023 report linking him to a fatal shooting.

After a nine-day trial, the eight-person jury determined that Spears was owed $9.25 million in damages.

Israeli Pm Netanyahu Initiating Defamation Lawsuit Against New York Times Over Controversial 'Dog Rape' Story

Spears was mentioned in the March 2023 report authored by New York Times sportswriter Billy Witz. Spears was falsely identified as being a passenger in the car at the site of a January 2023 shooting that resulted in the death of 23-year-old Jamea Harris.

The Times issued a lengthy editor's note to the report in June 2023, but only after Spears filed the defamation lawsuit at the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Alabama.

"The original version of this article, published March 15, misidentified the person who was in the car with [Crimson Tide star player] Brandon Miller when the shooting occurred," the note began.

"Based on information from a person familiar with the case, the article erroneously identified that person as Kai Spears, a freshman basketball player. After the article was initially published, Alabama's athletic director and Spears's father denied that Spears was present. The Times included those responses and reviewed its reporting, but did not conclude that any other change to the article was warranted at that time.

"On Wednesday, Spears filed a defamation suit against The Times that included new details about the incident. Based on that information, editors assigned further reporting, which determined that the other person at the scene was not Spears but Cooper Lee, a student manager for the team. The Times regrets the error in the initial report."

Jury Finds Cnn Committed Defamation Against Navy Veteran, Settlement Reached In Punitive Damages

Witz, who began reporting for The Times in 2008, relied on one anonymous source who claimed Spears was at the site of the shooting. Witz testified the source was a "high-level person, professional."

"I think the way I was looking at it, Source A, by their job title and by virtue of their access to the transcript, videos and impound photos, was somebody who knew a lot about this case," Witz said, according to a report from The Tuscaloosa Patch.

"In my mind, the story had a focus, and this tragedy, as bad as it was, could have been much worse."

A separate anonymous source had told Witz, "I can tell you it's a White guy on the basketball team, I just don't remember his name," according to Witz's testimony.

According to The Patch, Witz ultimately conceded from the witness stand, "Yes, [the story] had a mistake, no question."

Reporter Who Exited Cnn After Being At Center Of Costly Defamation Trial Lands At Al Jazeera English

The Times noted in its own report about the verdict that it had not lost a defamation lawsuit brought in the United States over one of its articles in more than 50 years.

"We're disappointed the jury found The Times liable for an honest mistake," a Times spokesperson told Fox News Digital. "We thank the jury for its service, but believe the verdict and award of damages are contrary to law and not supported by the evidence. We are reviewing our legal options."

Spears' legal team did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

title: Former Washington QB gets next NFL shot with New York Giants
description: Former Washington Huskies quarterback Jake Haener signed with the New York Giants on Monday, where he will compete for a backup job.
fullText:
Jake Haener has earned another shot at an NFL roster.

The former Washington quarterback, who was taken in the fourth round of the 2023 NFL draft by the New Orleans Saints after transferring from Montlake to Fresno State, signed with the New York Giants on Monday morning. It's Haener's third team in 2026 after finishing the 2025 regular season on the Saints practice squad, then signing a reserve/futures contract with the Kansas City Chiefs before being waived in May.

The #Giants are signing veteran QB Jake Haener, source says. Haener, who had worked out for the team late last month, lands in East Rutherford after a few workouts with other teams. pic.twitter.com/s0TjX8Iojo

Haener appeared in only 4 games at Washington, all in 2018, completing 9 of his 13 passes for 107 yards with 1 touchdown and 1 interception. He nearly returned to the Huskies in 2022; however, after Washington hired Fresno State coach Kalen DeBoer to replace Jimmy Lake. DeBoer wanted Haener to follow him back to Montlake, but a credits issue and the subsequent re-hire of Jeff Tedford at Fresno State kept Haener with the Bulldogs. DeBoer pivoted to Indiana quarterback Michael Penix Jr., whom he had coached as the Hoosiers' offensive coordinator in 2019.

That decision, of course, worked out for Washington. Penix went on to become a Heisman finalist and led the Huskies to a national championship game appearance in 2023 before being selected No. 8 overall by the Atlanta Falcons in the 2024 NFL draft.

Haener has played in 8 NFL games, starting 1, all for the Saints in 2024. He has completed 18 of 39 career passing attempts for 226 yards with a touchdown and an interception. But after Giants third-string quarterback Brandon Allen struggled in the team's first preseason game, Haener has a real opportunity to win that job and join second-year passer Jaxson Dart and veteran backup Jameis Winston in New York's quarterback room.

After transferring to Fresno State, Haener set the program record for career completion percentage at 68.1 percent, finished in the top five of every major passing statistic, earned All-Mountain West honors twice, was named a captain all three years, and was named MVP of the 2023 Senior Bowl. He is one of three Bulldogs to throw for at least 4,000 yards in a season, along with brothers David and Derek Carr.

The Giants travel to Florida to play the Miami Dolphins on Saturday for their second of three preseason games. New York ends their preseason with a crosstown game against the New York Jets on August 28, two days before the 53-man roster deadline.

fullText:
Exclusive: Planning documents show datacentre in North Ockendon would be incompatible with UK net zero targets

A “hyperscale” datacentre in outer London would generate more than 1m tonnes of carbon dioxide a year, equivalent to the carbon footprint of 27,000 flights from London to New York, planning documents show.

The East Havering Data Centre Campus (EHDCC) in North Ockendon would be one of the largest datacentres in Europe if approved by Havering council, using 218 hectares of green belt to run servers and data storage systems for AI and cloud computing. Its developer, Digital Reef, has described the scheme as “a unique opportunity to create a sustainable datacentre campus of the future”.

But in the planning application, Digital Reef says the £14.7bn project “does not align with a science-based 1.5C compatible trajectory and achieving net zero by 2050”. Documents estimate the development would generate more than 72m tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) over its projected 60-year lifespan – 1.2m tonnes annually once fully operational.

Guardian analysis of planning documents for the dozens of proposed datacentres in the UK shows that the EHDCC has the highest projected carbon emissions disclosed by a developer.

Donald Campbell, advocacy director at the tech justice nonprofit Foxglove, said the EHDCC’s projected emissions were “staggering”.

“It’s a big threat to the ability to decarbonise in the UK,” he said. “It’s also going to be a big drain on important resources that are needed by homes and other businesses.”

According to Ofgem, the average UK household electricity consumption is 2,500 kWh per year. Digital Reef said in its proposal that at a “likely” 50% load, the campus would consume 2.65bn kWh per year of electricity, equivalent to the demand of more than 1m UK households.

The campus would be powered primarily by a huge 600MVA connection to the National Grid via the nearby Warley substation. Because the existing site does not have sufficient capacity, major upgrades are planned, including a new 400kV National Grid substation and a new 132kV UK Power Networks facility on adjacent land, with the full connection expected by 2033.

The 1.2m tonnes of CO₂e the EHDCC expects to emit would amount to 26,795 long-haul flights from London Heathrow to New York’s John F Kennedy international airport, according to the UN’s International Civil Aviation Organization’s carbon calculator.

North Ockendon Residents Association said the development would be a “massacre” of green belt land. “It’s crop-producing farmland, in an age when we are threatened by security, it’s the loss of wildlife habitats, and there’s the pollution cost, which everyone seems to brush under the carpet,” a group spokesperson said.

The scale of datacentre emissions raises questions over how Britain’s rapid expansion of AI infrastructure can be reconciled with the government’s legally binding climate targets.

The government designated datacentres as “critical national infrastructure” in 2024, putting the tech developments on an equal footing with water, energy and emergency services systems.

In January, planning legislation was amended so datacentre developers were able to apply as nationally significant infrastructure projects, meaning they were able to largely bypass the local authority planning procedure and seek approval directly from government.

Neso, Britain’s grid operator, has warned MPs that datacentre developers have requested 72.8GW of electricity connections by 2039 – a “huge step change for the sector” and nearly 60% more than the UK’s peak power demand last year – in a surge driven by the race to build AI and hyperscale infrastructure.

The government said last year the now disbanded department for science, innovation and technology (DSIT) would produce a national policy statement for the sector, but it has not yet been published.

Campbell said: “The government needs to be taking concrete steps to make sure that the public and the environment aren’t left to carry the social environmental costs of the datacentres. These datacentres are ultimately going to be serving the wealthiest companies in the world – so they need to be required to carry that cost.”

Planning documents said that where the zero-carbon target cannot be met on site, “any shortfall would be provided through a cash in lieu contribution to the borough’s carbon offset fund”. The developer estimates that payment at about £77.6m.

Campbell said datacentre developers should at a minimum be required to build enough additional renewable generation and storage to supply their facilities. “That’s the only way of really ensuring that it’s not going to add to carbon emissions,” he said. “They shouldn’t just plug into the grid and drain the power that everyone else needs.”

The first round of consultation on the EHDCC closed in April. A revised proposal reflecting any accepted changes is expected to be published for a further public consultation in the autumn.

Councillor Keith Prince, Reform UK leader of Havering council, said that as a decision on EHDCC is made by the local planning authority, it would be “wrong” to comment until that decision was made.

Digital Reef did not respond to request for comment.

title: Brian Burns: New York Giants' run defense 'dominant' in practice vs. Miami
description: The New York Giants "dominated" the Miami Dolphins in practice on Thursday, says Brian Burns.
fullText:
Spider-Man is unstoppable these days, not only at the box office, where the Marvel movie is crushing records, but on the field with the New York Giants defense.

But that's not Tom Holland out there in Blue. It's Giants edge rusher Brian Burns, who fancies himself after the iconic superhero. He's crushing it, too.

On Thursday, during a joint practice with the Miami Dolphins at their facility, the Baptist Health Training Center, which is located across the road from Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Burns led a relentless torrent of blue shirts into the opposing backfield.

Brian Burns said the Giants defense was "dominant." They could do better but the Dolphins couldn't stop them. 

Burns was told they had six sacks. He disagreed. He said it was more. pic.twitter.com/dNxcGa9rxX

The Giants have an embarrassment of pass-rushing options this year, so many that stud rookie Arvell Reese is being deployed as an off-ball linebacker rather than on the outside. Burns is the leader of the group that can "get after it."

Abdul Carter, who is on the cusp of possible greatness, mans the opposite flank from Burns. Behind him is veteran Kayvon Thibodeaux. Behind Burns is another very capable vet, Chauncey Golston.

The Dolphins are a rebuilding team under a first-time head coach, Jeff Hafley. They are not expected to win many games this season. They were no match for this group that the Giants general manager Joe Schoen constructed.

Big takeaway in Dolphins-Giants joint practice:

Giants pass rush looks eye-popping dominant. Physical, fast, deep.

Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, Kayvon Thibodeaux, Arvell Reese — hell of a quartet. They just swarm. Jevón Holland had a strong win with 3rd down sack off edge blitz.

Carter is coming, and Reese is on the tarmac. Burns is the star, though. His peers around the league have taken notice. The 28-year-old has recorded 71.0 sacks in seven seasons in the NFL, with at least 7.5 in each of them.

More are coming from Spider-Man.

title: Speedboat driver in fatal New York Harbor capsizing was in the US illegally, authorities say
description: The pilot of a speedboat that capsized during a tour around the Statue of Liberty, drowning an infant and her mother, has been arrested by U.S. immigration authorities who say he was in the country il...
fullText:
NEW YORK (AP) — The pilot of a speedboat that capsized during a tour around the Statue of Liberty, drowning an infant and her mother, has been arrested by U.S. immigration authorities who say he was in the country illegally.

Manuel Ernesto Hernandez-Umana, who has a pending federal criminal case in connection with the Aug. 8 crash, lied to a border officer and falsely claimed he was a U.S. citizen when he entered the country in Texas in 2007, the Department of Homeland Security said Wednesday.

Hernandez-Umana, 46, a citizen of El Salvador, is being held at a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention facility in Elizabeth, New Jersey, according to online records. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said he will eventually be deported.

Immigration authorities arrested him after he was released on bail in his criminal case, where he is charged with causing the deaths of 5-month old Antonella Garcia and 27-year-old Sara Sanchez through misconduct or neglect.

According to prosecutors, Hernandez-Umana wasn't licensed by the U.S. Coast Guard, wasn't aware of basic safety rules and told investigators he'd borrowed his friend's personal vessel for the New York Harbor excursion. The boat was illegally chartered and overcrowded, prosecutors said.

"Once he faces justice for his crimes, we will make sure that he is swiftly removed from our country," Mullin said in a statement.

Hernandez-Umana's lawyer, Amy Gallicchio, declined comment.

Hernandez, who had been living in Manville, New Jersey, was not required to enter a plea at his initial court appearance in the criminal case on Aug. 10. He wiped his eyes as he arrived to the courtroom, still wearing the T-shirt, swim trunks and water shoes he'd had on during the voyage. He is due back in court on Sept. 9.

According to Coast Guard investigators, Hernandez was piloting a 21-foot Yamaha AR210 with 14 people aboard — well over its 10 person capacity — when it swamped and sank as it made a U-turn in choppy waters. The tour began around 7 p.m. and the vessel capsized more than three hours into its journey.

The infant wasn't wearing a life preserver because the boat didn't have any for small children, prosecutors said. Instead, Hernandez told Sanchez she needed to wear a life vest and hold the infant throughout the hourslong tour, a violation of federal regulations, prosecutors said.

The tour was organized through Zeus Luxury Rental Inc., which advertises its services on social media platforms including Instagram and TikTok. A boat chartered by the company caught fire last year during a birthday cruise on Long Island Sound.

According to his criminal complaint, Hernandez told investigators he had worked for Zeus Luxury on a freelance or contract basis since last year, starting as a limousine driver. He said that twice recently he used his personal boat, a slightly larger Yamaha AR250, but used a friend's boat on Aug. 8 because his needed repairs, the complaint said.

Messages seeking comment were sent to a phone number and email address listed on Zeus Luxury's website. The phone number's voicemail was full, according to an automated recording.

title: NY Giants-Miami Dolphins joint practice: ‘Rules of engagement’ will be in place
description: John Harbaugh wants players on both teams to protect each other.
fullText:
Recently, I was listening to Sirius XM NFL Radio while driving to New York Giants practice. The host of the show (I see you, Bob Papa) was basically doing play-by-play of the fights breaking out during a joint practice between the New York Jets and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

I relay that story because fights seem to be commonplace during these joint practices, and the Giants are participating in one with the Miami Dolphins on Thursday in Miami.

Joint practices, of course, are not the controlled situations teams can create for their players during normal practices.

With that in mind, I asked Giants head coach John Harbaugh, a veteran of many of these situations, if there was a way a head coach could try to keep his players safe during a situation where he isn't in charge of every player on the field.

Welcome to the 'Rules of Engagement'.

"We'll have rules of engagement, we'll call it," Harbaugh said. "Talked to Coach Hafley. He talks to his team. We talk to our team. We have the same rules of engagement."

Harbaugh said those rules will include, and probably emphasize, that defenders getting anywhere the opposing quarterback is strictly verboten.

"It'll be the same that we use in our practice. It'll be probably more to the quarterback," Harbaugh said. "We'll emphasize protecting each other's quarterbacks even more, because as soon as somebody gets close, and the other team's going to talk about getting close, and we can't have that, nobody can get close to the quarterback. That's going to be a major point of emphasis."

There will be other rules of engagement.

"We're going to stay off the ground, and we're going to be looking for no blindside shots of any kind. We're not looking for that," Harbaugh said." It's a front-up tackle. That's kind of a front-up type of thud, wrap you can do, but it won't be side shots and things like that. That's the goal.

"So, we want to protect them as much as we protect our own players, and we want them to protect our players as much as they would protect their own players."

This will be a single practice in advance of Saturday's preseason game. What is Harbaugh's goal?

"I'm looking to get a good practice against a different team," Harbaugh said. "You get an opportunity to go against different players, different schemes, and evaluate your guys along those lines. It's good. It's just nice to see a different format, different plays, different players.

"And it's fun. It's more interesting. It's not another practice day for the guys. They're going against a new team."

Nabers, on the comeback trail from a pair of surgeries to repair a torn ACL, just began participating in a handful of team drills this week. He has been wearing a red, non-contact jersey.

Nabers will travel with the Giants to Miami, but won't take part in team drills on Thursday or play in Saturday's preseason game.

The Giants want to get Nabers involved in some degree of physicality in a controlled practice setting before exposing him to defenders on other teams.

"He won't go through the rest of the summer in a red jersey," Harbaugh said. "No, he'll be out of a red jersey before he plays in a game. He's going to have to get bumped around and hit and fronted up so he knows how to, you just have to feel that and know how to deal with it to protect yourself."

That just isn't going to happen in Miami.

title: Watch: Padres' Fernando Tatis Jr. robs grand slam, homers twice vs. Mets

fullText:
Aug. 19 (UPI) -- Fernando Tatis Jr. homered twice and performed an immaculate grand slam robbery to help the San Diego Padres beat the New York Mets in Flushing, N.Y.

The All-Star outfielder homered in the first and fifth innings of the 5-2 triumph Tuesday at Citi Field. He stole a would-be grand slam from shortstop Francisco Lindor in the bottom of the second.

"He doesn't just do it," Padres manager Craig Stammen told reporters. "He does it with a flair."

The Padres, who have won eight of their last 10 games, remain in the lead for the third wild card slot. They hold a two game lead on the Arizona Diamondbacks for the National League's final playoff ticket.

Tatis started his exploits by hitting the first pitch of the night to left field for a 452-foot home run. The Mets attempted to rally in the bottom of the next inning. Padres starter Robbie Ray started the frame with walks issued to designated hitter Francisco Alvarez and first baseman Christopher Morel. Second baseman Marcus Semien flew out in the next at-bat.

Ray proceeded to walk left fielder A.J. Ewing to load the bases. Lindor walked to the plate two at-bats later. He watched a Ray changeup miss the zone for a ball. He then smacked a 1-0 sinker deep to right field.

Tatis watched the ball cruise 337 feet toward the right field corner. He left his feet over the warning track and reached his gloved left hand high over the wall before snagging the ball. Tatis landed and celebrated the catch by flipping the ball out of his glove and into his right hand.

He returned to the plate in the top of the fifth to face Mets starter Zac Thornton for a third time. The Padres slugger unloaded on a 2-1 fastball, sending the pitch to right center for a 379-foot, two-run blast.

Catcher Luis Torrens hit a 417-foot solo shot for the Mets' first run to lead off the bottom of the fifth. Padres first baseman Ty France responded with an RBI single in the top of the seventh.

Center fielder Luis Robert Jr. drove in the Mets' final run with a 390-foot solo shot in the bottom of the eighth. Padres third baseman Manny Machado hit a 397-foot solo homer in the top of the ninth for the game's final run.

Ray allowed just three hits and one run over six innings to improve to 11-7 this season. Thornton surrendered six hits and three runs over five innings to drop to 3-4.

Tatis went 2 for 5 with three RBIs, two runs scored and a strikeout. He hit .280 with 15 home runs, 28 stolen bases and 60 RBIs through his first 125 games this season.

The Padres (68-59) remain in second place in the National League West, eight games behind the division-leading Los Angeles Dodgers (76-51).

The Mets (57-70) remain in last place in the National League East, 17.5 games behind the division-leading Atlanta Braves (74-52).

title: Venus Williams given US Open singles wildcard - will Serena join her?
description: Venus Williams is given a wildcard for the US Open singles aged 46 - and 29 years after she made her New York debut.
fullText:
Venus Williams has been given a wildcard for the US Open singles - and sister Serena could potentially still join her with one spot remaining.

Venus, 46, first played in New York 29 years ago and reached the final on her singles debut in 1997.

The American won two of her seven Grand Slam singles titles at Flushing Meadows in 2000 and 2001.

Venus and 2017 champion Sloane Stephens have been given direct entry into the main draw which begins on Sunday, 30 August.

Serena returned to tennis in June, four years after "evolving away" from the sport, and played in singles at Wimbledon.

The sisters were due to play doubles together at SW19 but withdrew after Serena, 44, injured her knee in her first-round loss to Maya Joint.

They made their return together at the Cincinnati Open on Tuesday, losing a thriller at the Cincinnati Open in three sets.

Wildcards for the women's doubles have yet to be announced, and there are three remaining places in the revamped mixed doubles competition that takes place from 24 August.

Elder sister Venus has played singles sporadically on the WTA Tour over the past four years but has lost all 10 of her matches this season and is winless in 13.

Her last singles win was in Washington in July 2025.

Venus did not play singles at Wimbledon and has played just one Grand Slam match this year - a first-round loss to Serbia's Olga Danilovic at the Australian Open.

Williams sisters lose on doubles return

Swiatek beats Rybakina for first title of season

Venus has fared better in doubles in recent years, reaching the quarter-finals in New York last year alongside Canada's Leylah Fernandez.

She has not won a singles match at a Grand Slam since Wimbledon in 2021, where she reached the second round.

However, the Williams sisters still draw huge crowds together or separately, with stands packed out in Cincinnati for their recent return.

Serena, a 23-time Grand Slam singles champion, played what was expected to be the last tournament of her career in New York in 2022.

However, she made her return first in doubles at Queen's in June before being given the final Wimbledon women's singles wildcard.

Venus won her first US Open singles title in 2000, two months after earning her maiden major at Wimbledon.

She beat Serena in the final a year later to defend her title - the first of nine major showpieces the sister would contest.

Venus became the oldest US Open singles player in 44 years when she played at the tournament last year.

She lost in three sets to ninth seed Karolina Muchova and gave an emotional news conference afterwards, saying it was "nice to be free".

In 2011, Williams was diagnosed with Sjogren's syndrome, an incurable autoimmune disease with symptoms including pain, numbness and fatigue.

She spoke in 2025 about the impact of painful fibroids - abnormal growths that develop in the uterus - on her daily life.

In the men's draw, France's Gael Monfils has been awarded a wildcard in the final Grand Slam of his career.

There is also one remaining wildcard for the men's singles, which could go to 2016 champion Stan Wawrinka.

The Swiss is also calling time on his career at the end of the year.

Venus may not have won a singles match for over a year, but she is at least appearing regularly - she has played singles and doubles in Washington, Toronto and Cincinnati in the last month alone.

Serena has some decisions to make.

The USTA appears to be holding a singles wildcard open for her, as the All England Club did ahead of Wimbledon.

But does she feel ready to play singles after such little preparation?

Serena's comeback has so far consisted of three doubles and one singles, while the match in Cincinnati was her first in seven weeks after her knee injury.

It seems likely we will see the sisters in the doubles, though - and Serena and Venus may not be the only ones interested in the spaces for next week's mixed doubles event.

Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz are back in training after knee and wrist injuries, but have not yet committed to playing in New York.

If they do feel ready to return to singles, then the mixed doubles tournament which precedes it may prove a nice way to ease back in.

fullText:
A New York democratic socialist lawmaker's referral to shoplifting being the result of a "biological need" is getting swift blowback.

New York state Assemblywoman Emily Gallagher suggested this week that aggressive prosecution of theft of items like soap and toothpaste was wrongheaded, saying the "true crime is that there is such incredible wealth disparity in this city that there are people who can be thrown in jail simply for having a biological need."

"This is exactly the wrong way to talk about crime and poverty. Poverty can help explain why someone commits an offense," former Palm Beach County State Attorney Dave Aronberg told Fox News Digital. "It should matter when prosecutors decide how to handle a case. But poverty is not a permission slip to steal."

Aronberg, who now leads his own law firm, rejected the suggestion that prosecution necessarily means incarceration and pointed to alternatives available for first-time offenders.

Soros Network Rebuilds Progressive Prosecutor Push After String Of Election Losses

"Suggesting that someone who steals toothpaste for the first time is automatically being thrown in jail creates a false picture of how the system actually works. Prosecution does not have to mean incarceration," Aronberg said. "There are diversion programs, treatment, conditional dispositions and other ways to impose accountability without ruining someone's life."

Retired New York Police Department Sgt. Joe Imperatrice, founder of Blue Lives Matter NYC and a retired NYPD supervisor with more than 20 years of law enforcement experience, said politicians should focus on crime victims rather than make excuses for offenders. He also defended the policing strategy Gallagher wants New York City to abandon.

"Broken Windows is a proven theory which holds people accountable for their actions and rightfully so," Imperatrice said. "The tides are turning and everyday New Yorkers are getting sick and tired of this reckless narrative."

Organizers said Court Watch NYC monitored 360 arraignments over four days and found more than half involved misdemeanor offenses.

Gallagher and her allies also urged Mayor Zohran Mamdani to end "broken windows policing." Mamdani entered office promising to shift some responses to homelessness, mental illness and low-level disorder away from police while maintaining enforcement against serious violent crime.

The NYPD reported retail theft declined 16.3% citywide during the first half of 2026 compared with the same period last year. The department attributed the decline to analyzing crime patterns, deploying officers at high-theft locations and conducting sustained investigations.

Aronberg also warned that Gallagher's argument could damage the Democratic Party politically by allowing Republicans to portray the party as unconcerned about crime.

fullText:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers UDFA Jack Pyburn was one of the clear winners of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' preseason win over the New York Jets. Pyburn recorded two pressures, which was enough to catch the attention of head coach Todd Bowles.

Bowles noted that Pyburn has been unable to get the attention he deserves in a crowded edge rusher room. However, he was quite pleased with the statement he made when things mattered.

"He did a heck of a job last night," Bowles said. "He showed up with the lights on. He's a solid player, doesn't get much run with all the other guys playing…he showed everybody who he was."

Bowles on undrafted rookie Jack Pyburn, who had two sacks Friday: "He did a heck of a job last night. He showed up with the lights on. He's a solid player, doesn't get much run with all the other guys playing … he showed everybody who he was."

— Greg Auman (@gregauman) August 15, 2026

Pyburn might be able to earn more chances to prove whether he belongs on the 53-man roster if he continues to catch the coaches' eyes like that.

GettyJack Pyburn #58 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Pyburn was undrafted out of LSU, mostly due to questionable physical tools. He showed very short arms at the NFL Combine. They are in the first percentile among players in the NFL. Considering an edge rusher depends highly on arms and reach, this turned plenty of teams off.

Still, he has been able to make a name for himself with a solid preseason. He played 25 snaps, with 16 being rush snaps. He defended the run on seven snaps and had two coverage snaps.

Those were his only two pressures, but he also had two run stops, per PFF. They gave him an overall grade of 71, with his tackling grade being a 74 and his pass rush grade being a 68.7. All three were above average. For what it is worth, his run defense grade was 62.5, which is considered average.

The big issue for Pyburn is that there are limited chances for him to climb the Bucs depth chart. We know that Rueben Bain and Yaya Diaby are going to start on the edge.

The team also signed Al-Quadin Muhammad, who will rotate in with those two. They also have David Walker, who was drafted last year. Walker missed his rookie season due to injury, but has been a presence throughout training camp.

He ran ahead of Pyburn in the preseason opener and looked strong. Anthony Nelson would slot in as the fifth rusher. He is a veteran and could be on the trade block if the Bucs feel good about Pyburn.

Still, last year he was one of their best rushers, so it is hard to see them pushing Pyburn over him. Things open up around the sixth edge rusher.

Mo Kamara is a UDFA entering his third year who is trying to stick around. Yasir Holmes is another rookie UDFA who is not flashing as much as Pyburn. Then, there is Chris Braswell, who has been a letdown since the Bucs drafted him.

If Pyburn does not make a roster push, he appears to be in good position to make the practice squad. He just needs to keep this up.

title: How many games is Giants coach John Harbaugh forecast to win in 2026?
description: How many games did NFL Media's Bucky Brooks forecast New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh to win in 2026?
fullText:
How successful will New York Giants coach John Harbaugh be in his first year with the team next season?

NFL.com's Bucky Brooks forecasts that Harbaugh will win the third-most games among all head coaches leading new teams in 2026.

It is no coincidence that the Giants have captured four Lombardi Trophies under the direction of hard-nosed coaches Bill Parcells and Tom Coughlin. The discipline and attention to detail demanded by those taskmasters brought the best out of blue-collar squads that knocked off heavyweights en route to Super Bowl triumph. Harbaugh's no-nonsense approach could produce similar results for Big Blue, with the Super Bowl-winning coach taking over a roster that has plenty of blue-chip talent on the defensive side of the ball. New DC Dennard Wilson's aggressive scheme will force opponents to contend with a front seven that could rival some of the best groups in franchise history. Although the offense must embrace an error-free approach that relies heavily on the running game and splash plays from quarterback Jaxson Dart, the Giants' ability to force opponents into street fights could make them the team nobody wants to face down the stretch.

Harbaugh has plenty of talent to work with in New York. The Giants have a player at every key position on offense, aside from the offensive line, who is likely to have a breakout year in 2026.

Jaxson Dart has the talent to exceed 3,500 passing yards and 500 rushing yards next season. Cam Skattebo is trending toward a 1,000-yard rushing season, while Malik Nabers is likely to produce like a top-five wide receiver in the NFL. Isaiah Likely ranks among the biggest breakout candidates in the league heading into the upcoming year.
